$comment: p15-oracle-075: the sidebar and workspaceGroup action families (every non-excluded id of plans/cmux-next/action-surfaces.json whose family_of is sidebar: 93 today, the design's 88 plus ids added since). gen_actions.py (p15-oracle-071) reads this file (load_tuning: only $comment and actions; each spec's keys in TUNING_KEYS) and writes one flat case per action; regeneration keeps it byte-stable. Each entry was reviewed against its handler (WorkspaceGroupHandlers, WorkspaceVerbHandlers, WorkspaceSetVerbs, WindowMembershipHandlers, StashHandlers, SidebarArchiveActions, SidebarSectionHandlers, SidebarHiddenSections, SidebarDensityActions, SidebarGroupByActions, SidebarWorkspaceTabsToggle, SidebarPriorityFeed, ProfileMenuHandlers). Legacy registry.bind handlers report action.done; the two archive toggles are bindEffect and name no receipt. Group actions act on the shown workspace's group, which each case makes first (make-group); section and item actions have no target kind in case-v1, so they run their typed refusal until p15-oracle-270, except the five section and item toggles, which are blocked live-value until then (gen_actions.py restores a toggle by running it again, which a refused toggle fails); the group's color, icon and archived mark are not facet fields until p15-oracle-271, and the items of the top band (Home, an added item) not until p15-oracle-272. sidebar.chat.togglePin's silent no-op with no target is p15-oracle-273's to fix. Not tuned: workspaceGroup.delete (excluded), the gaps workspaceGroup.addToSection, workspaceGroup.moveToSpace and sidebar.priority.* (p15-oracle-086), workspaceGroup.moveToWindow (its window argument is a live value), and the destructive workspaceGroup.closeWorkspaces, workspaceGroup.closeOthers, sidebar.section.remove, sidebar.section.closeWorkspaces and sidebar.layout.reset (the sweep's plan blocks them by flag). Chromium: a case per command on one fixture browser, as chrome/browser/ui/tabs/tab_strip_model_unittest.cc tests each TabStripModel command on its own model; the sidebar facet reads the model the same way (SidebarSnapshot.oracleFacet).
